subject: physics
question_text: Define gravitational potential and gravitational potential energy. Obtain an expression for the gravitational potential energy of a body of mass m at a distance r from a body of mass M.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two definitions
lines: Gravitational potential ENERGY of a body at a
point is the work done in bringing it from
Gravitational POTENTIAL at the point is that
same work per unit mass: V = U / m.
steps.why: Potential belongs to the point in space; potential energy belongs to the body you put there.
common_mistakes: Using the two words as if they meant the same thing.

recall.must_convey: That potential energy is the work done from infinity to the point, and potential is that work per unit mass.
reject: integrating the force from infinity to r

steps.label: The work done
lines: At a distance x from the mass M the pull on the
This force is not constant, so the work must be
integrated. Integrating F over x from infinity
down to r gives the work done BY the pull:
steps.why: A 1/x² force integrates to a 1/x energy — one power of x is lost to the integration, which is why U goes as 1/r and not 1/r².
common_mistakes: Multiplying force by distance directly, which is only valid for a constant force.

recall.must_convey: That the force G M m by x squared is integrated from infinity down to r, giving G M m by r.
accept: integrate the force from infinity to r

steps.label: The result
lines: The potential energy is the work done AGAINST
the pull, which is the negative of this:

lines.text: U = − G M m / r,     V = − G M / r

lines: Both are taken as zero at infinity, by choice.
steps.why: The zero is a convention, but the DIFFERENCE between two points is not — and only differences are ever measured.
common_mistakes: Giving U as positive, which would mean the masses repel.

recall.must_convey: That U is minus G M m by r and V is minus G M by r, both zero at infinity.
accept: minus G M m by r
reject: integrate the force from infinity to r
